summary: Partial source-based extraction of the almost-algebra/Galois foundations and the ramified almost-purity proof. Reuse PerfectoidSpaces P0–P3; separate ramified Riemann extension, almost-perfectoid inverse limits and the Abhyankar envelope. Full extraction of Sections 2–3, applications and baseline verification remains required.

items.name: An almost base with a flat tensor square
items.statement: An almost base is a commutative ring V with an ideal m satisfying m²=m and such that m⊗_V m is flat over V. The ideal m is an explicit input; it need not be a valuation-ring maximal ideal.

items.name: Base change of the almost-base condition
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m) and a ring map V→V′, the extended ideal mV′ is idempotent and its tensor square over V′ is flat.

items.name: Flat compatible-root ideals
items.statement: If π is a non-zero-divisor in V with a chosen compatible system π^(1/p^n), the ideal generated by all π^(1/p^n) is flat and idempotent; in particular it satisfies the almost-base condition.

items.name: The almost-module category
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m), form Vᵃ-Mod by localizing V-Mod at morphisms whose kernel and cokernel are killed by m, equivalently the Serre quotient by modules M with mM=0. This is an abelian category.

items.name: Almost injectivity, surjectivity and isomorphisms
items.statement: A V-linear map is almost injective, almost surjective, or an almost isomorphism when its kernel, cokernel, or both, respectively, are annihilated by m. These correspond to monomorphisms, epimorphisms, and isomorphisms after almostification.

items.name: Almostification and its two module adjoints
items.statement: Writing m̃=m⊗_V m, the exact localization M↦Mᵃ has right adjoint N↦N_*=Hom_{Vᵃ}(Vᵃ,N) and left adjoint N↦N_!=m̃⊗_V N_*. One has (N_*)ᵃ≅N, (Mᵃ)_*≅Hom_V(m̃,M), and Hom_{Vᵃ}(Mᵃ,Nᵃ)≅Hom_V(m̃⊗_V M,N). Almostification preserves limits and colimits.

items.name: Detecting almost epimorphisms on almost elements
items.statement: For a morphism N→N′ of almost V-modules, the morphism is an epimorphism if and only if N_*→N′_* is almost surjective. The right adjoint (-)_* is not asserted to be right exact.

items.name: Mittag–Leffler for almost modules
items.statement: For an inverse sequence (N_n) of almost V-modules with epimorphic transition maps, lim_n N_n→N_0 is an epimorphism.

items.name: Countable derived inverse limits
items.statement: The almost-module category is complete and cocomplete and products preserve epimorphisms. For inverse sequences, and hence inverse systems admitting a countable cofinal chain, higher inverse limits vanish in degrees greater than one. Almostification commutes with lim¹, computed by the usual product telescope cokernel.

items.name: Adically complete almost Nakayama
items.statement: Let I be an ideal of V and f:M→N a morphism of I-adically complete almost V-modules. If M/IM→N/IN is an epimorphism, then f is an epimorphism. The proof uses the graded pieces, surjectivity on the kernels of successive quotients, and almost Mittag–Leffler.

items.name: Almost algebras and module categories
items.statement: Almost V-algebras are commutative monoid objects of Vᵃ-Mod. For an almost algebra A construct A-Mod, A-Alg and the relative tensor product. Almostification on algebras has the right adjoint (-)_* and a left adjoint (-)_!!; the latter is distinct from the module left adjoint.

items.name: Limits, coproducts and idempotents for almost algebras
items.statement: Almost-algebra categories have small limits and colimits. Relative tensor products are coproducts, and (B⊗_A C)ᵃ≅Bᵃ⊗_{Aᵃ}Cᵃ for ordinary V-algebras. Finite product decompositions are described by complete orthogonal idempotent systems in the ring of almost elements.

items.name: Extensions of almost algebras
items.statement: A morphism A→B of almost V-algebras is a monomorphism precisely when A_*→B_* is almost injective. Such monomorphisms are the extensions used in the almost Galois arguments.

items.name: Changing the almost base
items.statement: For a ring map V→V′ carrying m into m′, restriction of scalars induces exact functors from (V′,m′)ᵃ-modules to (V,m)ᵃ-modules and corresponding functors on almost algebras and their module categories. For the relative categories on a fixed underlying algebra these are equivalences when the image of m generates m′. Include the natural comparison of almost-element functors.

items.name: Flat and faithfully flat almost modules and maps
items.statement: An almost A-module M is flat when -⊗_A M is exact. A→B is faithfully flat when extension of scalars is exact and faithful. Equivalently for a map of almost algebras, it is a monomorphism and B/A is flat.

items.name: Transport and filtered colimits of almost flat extensions
items.statement: Flatness or faithful flatness of A_*→B_* implies the corresponding almost property; faithful flatness is equivalent to faithful flatness for the algebra left-adjoint map. Filtered colimits of flat, respectively faithfully flat, extensions retain the corresponding property.

items.name: Almost finite projectivity by approximate retracts
items.statement: An almost A-module P is finite projective in André’s convention if, for every η∈m, there are n and maps P→A^n→P whose composite is η·id_P. This is the almost, not ordinary, finite-projective condition.

items.name: Homological characterization of almost finite projectivity
items.statement: The approximate-retract condition is equivalent to almost projectivity, expressed by annihilation by m of all positive Ext groups into any module, together with almost finite generation: for every η∈m there is A^n→P with cokernel killed by η.

items.name: Flatness of almost projective modules
items.statement: Every almost projective module is flat. A faithful almost projective A-module, with faithfulness defined by the monomorphism A→End(P)ᵃ, is faithfully flat.

items.name: Exterior powers and trace for almost finite projectives
items.statement: Exterior powers of an almost finite-projective A-module remain almost finite projective. Construct its trace morphism (End P)ᵃ→A and define constant rank r by Λ^(r+1)P=0 and invertibility of Λ^r P.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent of almost finite projectivity
items.statement: For a faithfully flat map A→A′ of almost algebras, P is almost finite projective over A if and only if P⊗_A A′ is almost finite projective over A′.

items.name: Completeness of almost finite projective modules
items.statement: If the almost algebra A is I-adically complete, every almost finite-projective A-module P is I-adically complete. The comparison P→lim_n P/I^nP has kernel and cokernel annihilated by every η∈m via approximate finite-free retracts.

items.name: Almost finite étale algebras
items.statement: An almost A-algebra B is finite étale when B is almost finite projective over A and multiplication B⊗_A B→B is projection onto a factor in a decomposition B⊗_A B≅B×C. Under finite projectivity the second condition is equivalent to flatness of multiplication.

items.name: Trace pairing for almost finite étale algebras
items.statement: For an almost finite étale A-algebra B, trace is compatible with base change and the pairing (b,c)↦Tr(bc) identifies B with its A-dual. If A→B is an extension, it is faithfully flat and trace is an epimorphism.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent of almost finite étaleness
items.statement: For a faithfully flat map A→A′ of almost algebras, B is almost finite étale over A if and only if B⊗_A A′ is almost finite étale over A′. The assertion also preserves a specified constant rank.

items.name: Reduction equivalence with its restricted almost ideal
items.statement: If m=π^(1/p^∞)V and the almost algebra A is π-adically complete, reduction modulo π is an equivalence from almost finite étale A-algebras to almost finite étale A/π-algebras. The special form of the almost ideal is part of the hypothesis and cannot be dropped in the ramified (ϖT) setting.

items.name: The finite Galois comparison map
items.statement: For a finite group G acting by A-algebra automorphisms of an almost A-algebra B, construct B⊗_A B→∏_{γ∈G}B by b⊗b′↦(γ(b)b′)_γ and the invariant almost algebra B^G as an equalizer.

items.name: Almost Galois extensions
items.statement: An extension A→B with a given finite group G of A-automorphisms is G-Galois if B^G=A and the comparison B⊗_A B→∏_G B is an isomorphism. These conditions may be tested with the right adjoint (-)_*, but do not imply that A_*→B_* is an ordinary Galois extension.

items.name: Almost Galois implies almost finite étale
items.statement: A G-Galois extension of almost algebras is almost finite étale of constant rank |G|. Its trace is the sum of the G-conjugates. The proof extracts η-scaled dual bases from the torsor idempotent for every η∈m.

items.name: Base change and descent of almost Galois extensions
items.statement: A G-Galois extension A→B stays G-Galois after arbitrary almost-algebra base change A→A′. Conversely, G-Galoisness descends along faithfully flat A→A′.

items.name: Intermediate almost Galois extensions
items.statement: Let A→B be G-Galois and A→C→B intermediate, with C→B H-Galois for H⊂G. Then C⊗_A B≅∏_{G/H}B, and C is almost finite étale of constant rank |G/H| over A.

items.name: A symmetric-group Galois envelope
items.statement: For an injective finite étale ring map R→S of positive constant rank r, construct R→T that is S_r-Galois and factors through S, such that S→T is S_(r−1)-Galois. Geometrically remove all partial diagonals from the r-fold fibre power of Spec S over Spec R.
items.note: An explicit auxiliary construction for the finite étale descent proof owned by P3. The extension and positive-rank hypotheses prevent misuse of the rank-zero factor; it is not a primitive field normal-closure theorem.

items.name: Rigidity inside a ring with a finite group action
items.statement: Let a finite group G act on a ring S and set R=S^G. If a G-stable intermediate subring R⊂S′⊂S is G-Galois over R, then S′=S.
items.note: Supplies the finite étale/Galois proof step of P3; it is also used in Proposition 4.4.4(3). The proof uses faithful-flat descent, not a dimension argument.

items.name: Almost morphisms between uniform Banach algebras
items.statement: For an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A, the category A^â-uBan has uniform Banach A-algebras as objects and Hom(B,C)=Hom_{A°ᵃ-Alg}(B°ᵃ,C°ᵃ). Its full subcategory A^â-pPerf consists of the almost-perfectoid objects. Here almostification uses the ideal generated by T^(1/p^n)K°° in the integral perfected-coordinate base.

items.name: Almost-perfectoid algebras
items.statement: A uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra B is almost perfectoid when B^â is isomorphic, in the category whose morphisms are maps between almost power-bounded algebras, to the image of a perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra. This does not assert that B itself is perfectoid.

items.name: Perfectoid coreflection after almostification
items.statement: The right adjoint B↦B^♮ to the inclusion of perfectoid algebras into uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebras induces a right adjoint after almostification. Restricted to almost-perfectoid objects, it is quasi-inverse to the inclusion of the almostified perfectoid category. The counit goes from B^♮ to B, not from B to B^♮.

items.name: Frobenius criterion for almost perfectoidness
items.statement: Let B be a uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra, and choose 0≠ϖ∈K°° with compatible p-power roots and |p|≤|ϖ|. Then B is almost perfectoid if and only if Frobenius on B°/ϖ is almost surjective for the ramified root ideal. Surjectivity here is equivalently almost surjectivity of the Frobenius-linearized module map, not an assertion that Frobenius is K°/ϖ-linear.

items.name: Integral counit criterion for almost perfectoidness
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 3.5.4, B is almost perfectoid if and only if (B^♮)°→B° is an almost isomorphism for the ramified root ideal.

items.name: Banach counit criterion for almost perfectoidness
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 3.5.4, B is almost perfectoid if and only if B^♮→B is an almost isomorphism, equivalently if some perfectoid Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra admits an almost-isomorphic continuous homomorphism to B.

items.name: Finite-group invariants of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: If a finite group G acts on a perfectoid K-algebra B by continuous K-algebra automorphisms, the invariant algebra B^G, with its induced Banach topology, is perfectoid. No assumption that |G| is invertible is imposed.

items.name: Tilting commutes with finite-group invariants
items.statement: For a finite group G acting continuously on a perfectoid K-algebra B, the canonical comparison (B^G)^♭→(B^♭)^G is an isomorphism of perfectoid K^♭-algebras.

items.name: Integral root-localization models
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid of residue characteristic p, with 0≠ϖ∈K°°, |p|≤|ϖ|, and compatible p-power roots. For r∈N[1/p] and a (K°/ϖ^r)[T^(1/p^∞)]-algebra R, set R[j]=R⊗_{K°[T^(1/p^∞)]}K°[T^(1/p^∞),(ϖ^j/T)^(1/p^∞)]. The transition R[j+1]→R[j] sends (ϖ^(j+1)/T)^s to ϖ^s(ϖ^j/T)^s for s∈N[1/p]. The coefficient ring on the right is the indicated subring of the Laurent perfected-coordinate algebra, not a completion.

items.name: Recovery from integral root-localization models
items.statement: For R and R[j] as in §4.2.1, the canonical map R→lim_j R[j] is an almost isomorphism for the base (K°[T^(1/p^∞)],(ϖT)^(1/p^∞)). No flatness assumption on R over the coordinate ring is added.

items.name: Compatible-root saturation
items.statement: For a uniform Banach K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A with g=T·1 a non-zero-divisor, define g^(-1/p^∞)A°={x∈A[1/g] : g^(1/p^n)x∈A° for every n≥0}=⋂_n g^(-1/p^n)A°. This is an intersection, not the union of the fractional lattices.

items.name: Perfectoid Riemann extension by an inverse limit
items.statement: Let A be an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra and g=T·1 a non-zero-divisor. With A[j]=A{ϖ^j/g}, the canonical comparison identifies lim_j A[j]° with g^(-1/p^∞)A°. The rational localizations carry their complete Banach topology; they are not the uncompleted algebraic localization A[1/g].

items.name: Root saturation as complete integral closure
items.statement: With A and g as in Theorem 4.2.2, g^(-1/p^∞)A° is the complete integral closure of A° in A[1/g]. Complete integral closure means closure under almost-integral elements, not merely topological closure or ordinary integral closure.

items.name: Largest perfectoid subalgebra in a principal localization
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.2.2, (g^(-1/p^∞)A°[1/ϖ])^♮ is the largest spectral perfectoid A-algebra contained in A[1/g] with continuous structure map. The perfectoid coreflection is part of this formula; it must not be silently removed.

items.name: Tilting the root-saturated integral algebra
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollary 4.2.4, let g^♭ be the element of A^♭ corresponding to the compatible roots of g. There is a canonical identification (g^(-1/p^∞)A°)^♭=(g^♭)^(-1/p^∞)(A^♭)°. This identifies the tilted integral algebra, without asserting that g^(-1/p^∞)A°[1/ϖ] is itself perfectoid in mixed characteristic.

items.name: Uniform inverse limit
items.statement: For an inverse system of uniform Banach K-algebras (A_α), its uniform inverse limit is the bounded inverse limit: A=(lim_α A_α°)[1/ϖ] with the topology defined by the integral inverse limit. For perfectoid A_α its perfectoid-category limit A′ has a canonical map A′→A. These limits are distinct constructions.
items.note: This checkpoint fixes the construction consumed by the ramified theorem. Its general Banach-category ownership must be reconciled with AdicSpacesPartII before the extraction is completed; the Part II route must import any existing general supplier.

items.name: When a uniform inverse limit is the perfectoid limit
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid of characteristic zero, let (A_α) be an inverse system of perfectoid K-algebras, and let A′→A be the comparison from its perfectoid limit to its uniform limit. Then A is perfectoid if and only if A′→A is an isomorphism.

items.name: An integral inverse-limit criterion for perfectoidness
items.statement: In Proposition 4.3.1 choose 0≠ϖ∈K°° with pK°⊂ϖK° and an element denoted ϖ^(1/p) of norm |ϖ|^(1/p). If lim_α(A_α°/ϖ)→lim_α(A_α°/ϖ^(1/p)) is almost surjective for (K°,K°°), then the uniform limit A is perfectoid. This is a sufficient condition; the proposition does not claim its necessity.

items.name: Ramified almost-perfectoid inverse-limit criterion
items.statement: Let (A_α) be an inverse system of perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebras in the characteristic-zero setting of Proposition 4.3.1, and A its uniform limit. If lim_α(A_α°/ϖ)→lim_α(A_α°/ϖ^(1/p)) is almost surjective for the ideal T^(1/p^∞)K°°, then A^♮→A is an almost isomorphism; hence A is almost perfectoid.

items.name: Integral reduction of the ramified uniform limit
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the ramified almost-perfectoid inverse-limit criterion in Remark 4.3.1, the map A°/ϖ→lim_α(A_α°/ϖ) is an almost isomorphism for the same ramified ideal.

items.name: Vanishing of the nested root-localization lim¹
items.statement: Use the root-localization construction R↦R[j] of §4.2.1. If (R_i) is an inverse sequence of (K°/ϖ^r)[T^(1/p^∞)]-algebras such that R_i[j]→R_j[j]←R_j are almost isomorphisms for every i≥j, then lim¹_j(R_jᵃ)=0 in the ramified almost category. The proof uses summable annihilator estimates, not an assumption that all transition maps are surjective.

items.name: Compatible perfectoid algebras on principal annuli
items.statement: For an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A, set A[j]=A{ϖ^j/g}. Form the category of inverse systems of perfectoid A[j]-algebras B_j for which B_i{ϖ^j/g}→B_j is an isomorphism whenever i≥j; morphisms are compatible algebra morphisms. Rational localization defines σ from A^â-pPerf to this category.

items.name: Almost perfectoidness of compatible annular limits
items.statement: For an object (B_j) of the compatible annular category in §4.4.2, its uniform inverse limit is an almost-perfectoid A-algebra. Perfectoidness without almostification is not asserted.

items.name: Localization and uniform-limit adjunction
items.statement: For the categories of §4.4.2, uniform inverse limit is right adjoint to σ. The unit is an isomorphism: ulim∘σ≅id on A^â-pPerf. Consequently σ is fully faithful. The theorem does not assert that σ is essentially surjective.

items.name: Annular tower from a finite étale punctured algebra
items.statement: Let A be as in §4.4.2 and B′ a finite étale A[1/g]-algebra. Give B_j=B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A[j] its canonical finite étale Banach topology. Each B_j is perfectoid and the system belongs to the compatible annular category.

items.name: Recovering the annular pieces of the finite étale envelope
items.statement: Let B′ and B_j be as in Proposition 4.4.4 and B=ulim_j B_j. Then the canonical comparison B{ϖ^j/g}→B_j is an isomorphism for every j. This effectivity assertion is for towers arising from B′, not for every compatible annular tower.

items.name: Recovering the punctured finite étale algebra
items.statement: With B=ulim_j(B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A[j]) as in Proposition 4.4.4, the canonical map B′→B[1/g] is an isomorphism. Its proof uses the perfect trace pairing for injectivity and the finite Galois-envelope argument for surjectivity.

items.name: The ramified almost base for Abhyankar’s lemma
items.statement: Fix a perfectoid field K of residue characteristic p and 0≠ϖ∈K°° with compatible p-power roots and |p|≤|ϖ|. Use V=K°[T^(1/p^∞)] and m=(ϖT)^(1/p^∞)V. For a K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra A put g=T·1. Statements using this almost base differ from statements using (K°,K°°), even though the two compare after g is inverted.

items.name: Ramified almost-perfectoid extension equivalence
items.statement: In the base of §5.1, let A be an almost-perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra and g=T·1. Inverting g is an equivalence from A^â-algebras that are almost perfectoid and finite étale after inverting g to finite étale A[1/g]-algebras. A quasi-inverse sends B′ to ulim_j(B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A{ϖ^j/g}); the unit and counit are the identifications proved in §§4.4–5.2.

items.name: Integral form of ramified extension
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 5.2.1, inverting ϖ gives an equivalence between complete A°ᵃ-algebras that are finite étale modulo every power p^m and finite étale after inverting g, and A^â-algebras that are almost perfectoid and finite étale after inverting g. The quasi-inverse is the almost power-bounded algebra. The source’s condition is finite étale modulo every p^m; it is not replaced by integral almost finite étaleness.

items.name: Almost finite étaleness modulo powers of p
items.statement: In the base of §5.1 let A be almost perfectoid and let B be a perfectoid A-algebra in which g is a non-zero-divisor. Assume B[1/g] is finite étale over A[1/g]. Then B°ᵃ/p^m is finite étale over A°ᵃ/p^m for every m∈N, using the ramified almost ideal (ϖT)^(1/p^∞).

items.name: Integral almost purity after inverting the discriminant
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.2.3, B°[1/g] is almost finite étale over A°[1/g] in the valuation-ring almost setting (K°,K°°). This uses a different almost ideal from the modulo-p^m assertion.

items.name: Root-saturated integral envelope of a finite étale algebra
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩-algebra, g=T·1 a non-zero-divisor, and B′ finite étale over A[1/g]. Put S=g^(-1/p^∞)A°. Define D° as the ordinary integral closure of S in B′ and D as the ordinary integral closure of S[1/ϖ] in B′. These constructions are over the given A-algebra map; that map is not assumed injective when B′ is not faithful.

items.name: Identification of the analytic and integral envelopes
items.statement: In the setting of §5.3, let C=ulim_j(B′⊗_{A[1/g]}A{ϖ^j/g}). Then C=D and C°=D°. This identifies an almost-perfectoid envelope; its perfectoid coreflection is a separate object.

items.name: Completeness of the integral envelope
items.statement: The ring D° of §5.3 is ϖ-adically complete. It is the ordinary integral closure of g^(-1/p^∞)A° in B′, with the inherited topology supplied by its identification with the power-bounded ring of the uniform limit.

items.name: Root saturation of the integral envelope
items.statement: For D° as in §5.3, D°=(ϖg)^(-1/p^∞)D° inside B′, with root saturation interpreted as an intersection of fractional lattices.

items.name: Comparison with the ordinary integral closure of A°
items.statement: The inclusion of the ordinary integral closure of A° in B′ into D° is an almost isomorphism for (K°[T^(1/p^∞)],T^(1/p^∞)K°°[T^(1/p^∞)]).

items.name: The maximal perfectoid Abhyankar envelope
items.statement: For D of §5.3, D^♮ is the largest perfectoid A-algebra contained in B′, with continuous A-algebra structure. Its localization after inverting g is B′. The maximal object is D^♮, not an assertion that the almost-perfectoid algebra D itself is perfectoid.

items.name: Almost-surjectivity of the ramified trace
items.statement: In the setting of §5.3 assume in addition that B′ is faithful as an A[1/g]-module. Then Tr_{B′/A[1/g]}(D°)⊂g^(-1/p^∞)A° is an almost isomorphism of modules for the ramified almost base. Equivalently the trace map on D° is almost surjective onto that root-saturated integral ring.

routes.reason: Section 1 provides general-base almost algebra and the Galois proof auxiliaries used in P3. Proposition 3.8.1 supplies finite-group invariants within P8. These are existing stage contracts, not new owners. The abstract base strengthens the field-only opening of the older integrated P0 decomposition without duplicating the current general P0 plan.

routes.title: Perfectoid rings and spaces, Part II: ramification and Riemann extension
routes.brief: Extend Perfectoid rings and spaces (PerfectoidSpaces) beyond its unramified P3 theorem, without rebuilding P0 almost mathematics, P1 tilting, P2 rational localization or P8 finite-group invariants. Import the general topological algebra from foundations of adic spaces (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces) and the appropriate tensor-product prefix of Adic spaces, Part II (AdicSpacesPartII), verifying its precise stage ownership before blueprinting. First construct the almost-Banach category for the explicitly specified ramified ideal (ϖT)^(1/p^∞), almost-perfectoid algebras and the right perfectoid coreflection. Do not identify that right adjoint with the prismatic universal perfectoidization of PerfectoidQuotients. Prove André Proposition 4.2.1 with its integral root-localization models, Theorem 4.2.2 identifying lim_j A{ϖ^j/g}° with the intersection g^(-1/p^∞)A°, and its complete-integral-closure assertion. Retain the non-zero-divisor and compatible-root hypotheses. Establish the inverse-limit Frobenius criterion with only the implication directions proved in Proposition 4.3.1; prove Proposition 4.4.1 by its summable annihilator estimates, rather than assuming surjective transition maps. Construct the compatible annular category and Theorem 4.4.2: localization is fully faithful with uniform-limit right adjoint and isomorphic unit, but arbitrary essential surjectivity is not an output. For B′ finite étale over A[1/g], prove all three parts of Proposition 4.4.4 and the recovery B[1/g]≅B′. The final categorical theorem is exactly Theorem 5.2.1: complete A°ᵃ-algebras finite étale modulo every p^m and after inverting g are equivalent, by inverting ϖ, to almost-perfectoid A^â-algebras finite étale after inverting g, and then to finite étale A[1/g]-algebras by inverting g. Prove separately Proposition 5.2.3 in its two different almost bases. Prove the identifications and maximality in Proposition 5.3.1, distinguishing the almost-perfectoid integral envelope D from the largest perfectoid A-algebra D^♮ in B′. State trace almost-surjectivity only when B′ is faithful. Preserve Questions 3.5.1, 4.4.3 and 5.2.2 as boundaries rather than theorem targets. Complete extraction of the source’s §2–3 foundations, examples and §5.4 application before this brief is approved; any general missing construction already owned elsewhere must be imported rather than retained here. The current item list is a checkpoint, not an exhaustive blueprint.
routes.reason: The read P0–P9 contracts cover perfectoid foundations and unramified almost purity but not the ramified saturation and extension theorem. PerfectoidQuotients Q2–Q4 instead cover prismatic universal perfectoidization, André flatness, and Zariski closed quotients. conventions.base: Unless a statement specifies (K°,K°°), ramified almostification uses (K°[T^(1/p^∞)],(ϖT)^(1/p^∞)), with 0≠ϖ∈K°°, |p|≤|ϖ| and chosen compatible p-power roots. Equivalent completed-coordinate base changes are those in the source.
